solution.body:
[IMG]

cos $θ$ = $\frac{\frac{R}{2}}{R}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $θ$ $= 60^{o}$

Acceleration of the charged particle at the point of its emergence,

text: In a double-slit experiment, green light (5303$A^{\circ }$) falls on a double slit having a separation of 19.44 $μ$m and a width of 4.05 $μ$m. The number of bright fringes between the first and the second diffraction minima is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For single-slit diffraction with slit width $a$, the first and second minima lie at $\sin θ=\dfrac{λ}{a}$ and $\sin θ=\dfrac{2λ}{a}$.

Double-slit interference maxima (slit separation $d$) lie at $d\sin θ=nλ$, so the interference order at any angle is $n=\dfrac{d\sin θ}{λ}$.

At the first diffraction minimum: $n=\dfrac{d}{a}=\dfrac{19.44μ\text{m}}{4.05μ\text{m}}=4.8$.

At the second diffraction minimum: $n=\dfrac{2d}{a}=9.6$.

The bright fringes between these two minima have orders $n=5,6,7,8,9$, and none of them falls on a diffraction minimum, so there are 5 bright fringes.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot

text: If speed (V), acceleration (A) and force (F) are considered as fundamental units, the dimension of Young's modulus will be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

Young's modulus (Y) = $\frac{\frac{F}{A}}{\frac{\Delta l}{l}}$

$\therefore$ [Y] = $\frac{\left [MLT^{-2}\right ]}{[L^{2}]}$ = [ $ML^{-1}T^{-2}$]

Let [Y] = [V]$^{x}$ [A]$^{y}$ [F]$^{z}$

$\therefore$ [ $ML^{-1}T^{-2}$] = 

[$LT^{-1}$]$^{x}$ [$LT^{-2}$]$^{y}$ [MLT$^{-2}$]$^{z}$

$\Rightarrow$ [ $ML^{-1}T^{-2}$] =

 [ $M^{z} L^{x + y + z} T^{-x -2y - 2z}$

For dimensional balance, the dimension on both sides should be same.

So, z = 1

x + y + z = -1 

$\Rightarrow$ x + y = -2 ........(1)

and -x -2y - 2z = -2

$\Rightarrow$ x + 2y = 0 ...........(2)

By solving those two equations we get,

x = -4 and y = 2

$\therefore$ [Y] $= V^{-4}A^{2}F^{1}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot

text:
A copper wire is wound on a wooden frame, whose shape is that of an equilateral triangle. If the linear
dimension of each side of the frame is increased by a factor of 3, keeping the number of turns of the coil per
unit length of the frame the same, then the self inductance of the coil:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a coil on the triangular frame of side $a$, with $n$ turns per unit length, cross-sectional area $A=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^{2}$ and winding length $\ell$, the self-inductance is

$L=μ_{0}n^{2}A\ell .$

The same copper wire, of fixed length $l_{w}$, is wound, so the number of turns is $N=\dfrac{l_{w}}{3a}$ and the winding length is $\ell =\dfrac{N}{n}=\dfrac{l_{w}}{3an}$.

Substituting,

$L=μ_{0}n^{2}\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^{2}\cdot \dfrac{l_{w}}{3an}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}μ_{0}nl_{w}}{12}a\propto a.$

With $n$ unchanged and $a$ increased 3 times, the self-inductance increases by a factor of 3.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Evening Slot
